## Findings by module

### vintage-reselling-4

- **refined** (ch-001.txt): Defra ivory guidance states the penalty for dealing without an exemption, or making it possible for someone else to, as a maximum fine of 250,000 pounds or up to 5 years' imprisonment. The course splits this into an unlimited fine on indictment and civil penalties up to 250,000 pounds; align the wording with the GOV.UK summary or cite the Act for the split.
- **extended** (ch-003.txt): Defra ivory guidance, standard exemptions (registration costs 20 pounds): a musical instrument made before 1975 with less than 20% ivory by volume; an item made before 3 March 1947 with less than 10% ivory by volume where all the ivory is integral; a portrait miniature made before 1918 with a surface area of no more than 320 square centimetres; a sale to a qualifying museum. An exemption certificate (250 pounds, about 3 months, and no sale until it arrives) is only for pre-1918 items of outstandingly high artistic, cultural or historic value, usually a rare and important example of its type. Module 4 names the two routes but not the standard exemption thresholds or costs.
- **extended** (ch-002.txt): Defra ivory guidance: a buyer must check an item is registered or certified exempt before taking ownership; you need no exemption to keep, give away, bequeath or lend an item without payment; walrus ivory is not a listed species but other rules may apply; a registration stops being valid once the item is sold, so a reseller must re-register before reselling (an exemption certificate stays valid).
- **extended** (ch-005.txt): Defra ivory guidance, evidence: you must provide evidence of age (dated receipt or bill, dated catalogue or article, a date mark, knowledge such as inheritance before the relevant date, written verification from an antiques specialist, curator or ivory dealer, or radiocarbon dating) and of percentage volume (by eye when clearly small, such as a keyhole escutcheon on a large piece of furniture, or by measurement); 'integral' means the ivory cannot be removed without difficulty or damage; added or replacement listed ivory must pre-date 1975 and be for restoration only. Links the ivory rule to module 3's dating-from-evidence method.
- **extended** (ch-006.txt): Defra ivory guidance: if you know an item contains ivory but not which species, you may register at your own risk and APHA will assume a listed species; each registration needs a description, how it meets the criteria, and 1 to 6 photos showing the whole item, where the ivory is and any serial numbers; keep the reference number to show the buyer.
